extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical philosophy; anyone studying Plato's Republic
extracted.subtask_description: Close reading and interpretation of Plato's account of the virtues (justice, temperance, courage, wisdom), the tripartite soul, and the correspondence between a just State and a just individual, as presented in Book IV–V of the Republic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-mastery / Temperance as rule of the better part
rubrics_metrics.description: When the better has the worse under control, a man is said to be master of himself; when the better principle is overwhelmed by the worse he is blamed and called the slave of self.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperance/self-mastery is praised when the rational or 'better' part rules the inferior desires; loss of that rule (due to bad education or association) is an anti-pattern—one becomes 'slave of self' and unprincipled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperance as harmony across the whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Temperance extends to the whole and runs through all the notes of the scale, producing a harmony of the weaker and the stronger and the middle class; it is the agreement of the naturally superior and inferior as to the right to rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperance is not localized (unlike courage or wisdom) but is a state-wide/whole-soul harmony: rulers and subjects agreeing about who should rule. Evaluate temperance by whether classes/parts accept their proper roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage (state and individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courage resides in a part only (the spirited/auxiliary element) and makes the State valiant; in individuals it is the spirit retaining the commands of reason about what to fear in pleasure and pain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess courage by whether the spirited element preserves the legally/ordinarily held true opinions about danger (in the State: soldiers' opinions), and whether an individual's spirit obeys reason under stress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wisdom (state and individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wisdom resides in the rulers (or the ruling/knowledgeable part) and is the knowledge which presides over and counsels for the good of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge wisdom by the rulers' (or individual's ruling part's) knowledge of what is for the interest of each part and of the whole; a wise State or person has rulers who 'know' the proper course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice (doing one's own business) — political/organizational form
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice in the State is that one man should practise one thing only—the thing to which his nature was best adapted; justice is doing one's own business and not being a busybody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a political arrangement as just if each class (trader, auxiliary/warrior, ruling/counsellor) performs its proper function without meddling in others' roles; the division of labour is the practical test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice (individual) — inner concord of soul parts
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual is just when the several elements of his nature do their own work: the rational principle rules, the spirited principle is its ally, and both govern the concupiscent/appetitive part; the just man 'is his own master and his own law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess individual justice by internal order and harmony—whether the three soul-parts are bound together so the person 'is no longer many, but has become one'—and whether actions preserve that harmonious condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/practical formulation of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Suits at law are decided on the ground that a man may neither take what is another's, nor be deprived of what is his own; justice is the having and doing what is a man's own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From a legalistic viewpoint, test justice by respect for property/rights: not taking others' possessions and not being unjustly deprived—this is the criterion used in adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of labour / role integrity as foundation of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: When a cobbler does the carpenter's work, or a trader attempts to force his way into the warrior or legislator class for which he is unfitted, the interchange and meddling is ruinous; the harm of one class meddling in another is the greatest harm to the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The anti-pattern of injustice is role-meddling and attempts to perform functions for which one's nature or training is unsuited; evaluate institutions and persons for adherence to role integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tripartite soul: rational, spirited, appetitive
rubrics_metrics.description: The soul contains (1) a rational principle which reasons about the better and worse, (2) a spirited principle (passion/thumos) allied sometimes with reason, and (3) the appetitive/concupiscent principle which loves and hungers and thirsts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this taxonomy to analyze actions and moral conflict: identify which soul-part is acting or in conflict (reason vs appetite vs spirit) and whether the spirit supports reason or desire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of spirit (thumos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spirit is distinct from desire and from reason; it often sides with reason in the conflict of the soul and can act as the natural auxiliary of reason when properly educated—examples include children's early display of spirit and the Leontius story (desire vs dread).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the spirited element is correctly allied (with reason) or corrupted (aligned with appetite); education and upbringing influence this alliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence of State-virtues and Individual-virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: The same qualities that make the State wise, temperate, courageous, and just are found in the individual, and in the same relations: therefore a just State corresponds to a just soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating notions of justice or virtue, check that the structural relations among classes in the State map cleanly to the soul's parts; success of the State-level model is judged by the clarity of this correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue and vice as health and disease of the soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue is the health and beauty and well-being of the soul; vice is the disease and weakness and deformity of the same. Good practices lead to virtue; evil practices to vice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read moral evaluation in medical/metaphorical terms: judge actions and policies by whether they produce soul-health (order, harmony) or soul-disease (disorder, meddlesomeness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Causality: just actions produce justice; unjust actions produce injustice
rubrics_metrics.description: Just actions cause justice, and unjust actions cause injustice—analogous to how health-producing causes make the body healthy and disease-producing causes make it diseased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral appraisal should consider consequences and habituation: repeated just acts cultivate a just soul; repeated unjust acts cultivate injustice—so practice and institutions matter for long-term character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of education (music and gymnastic) in harmonizing the soul
rubrics_metrics.description: The united influence of music and gymnastic will bring the rational and spirited parts into accord, nerve and sustain reason with noble words and lessons, and moderate and civilize the wildness of passion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational regimen is a criterion for whether the soul/State will be virtuous: evaluate curricula, upbringing, and cultural practices by their capacity to harmonize soul-parts (nurture reason, civilize spirit, restrain appetite).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typology of States and corresponding soul-forms
rubrics_metrics.description: There are five forms of the State and five corresponding forms of the soul; the good/true City is called monarchy or aristocracy when governors are properly trained, and other (evil) forms follow in succession (four evil forms are to be noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the typology as a diagnostic rubric: identify which form a State or soul exhibits (the good form versus the corrupt forms) by checking training of rulers, role-order, and presence/absence of internal harmony; the text promises an ordered account of the degenerations to follow.
